title: The Cotton Club chorus girls and his wife
summary: Greer praises the chorus and says his wife was a lead dancer.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: a natural Broadway show like these shows on Broadway nowadays, ain't nothing. They ain't nothing. Them girls stopped the show. Oh, just the girls, the chorus. Stopped them cold. You to follow them girls! had to be somebody and know what you were doing. Sixteen of them, they were handpicked, like you pick a beauty contest. He screened them. That's how he picked them girls. / The prettiest colored girls in the world. They looked pretty on the stage and when they are on the street, down on Broadway shopping, people would turn around and look at them. They never seen nobody like that. That was the Cotton Club girls, famous.

You better believe they could dance! Wasn't -- all due respect to the Rockettes, but these girls were something else. Something else, boy, you better believe it, and they would look at the band, like they wasn't nothing. Because they made plenty of money, couldn't nobody hit on them, because they had their pocketbook full of money. They needed the somebody like hole in the head, that's right. My wife was one of the Cotton Club girls. She couldn't see me with a telescope. (Laughter)
My wife couldn't see me with a telescope and she was one of the lead dancers. That's right.
Jimmy Crawford's wife was one of the dancers, too.
